messages.subject: Re: RHEL PostgreSQL Install
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thank you for the report.
Do you have pg_config in your PATH?

The place of library and headers are assumed to available by
pg_config --includedir
pg_config --libdir

Best regards,
Tomoaki
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan


On 2013/11/30, at 0:52, Ted Rosenbaum wrote:

> Hello,
> 
> I had problems installing RPostgreSQL on RHEL 6 with a PostgreSQL 9.3 installation from the PostgreSQL yum repositories (http://yum.postgresql.org/repopackages.php#pg93).  
> 
> The problem was that the installation script could not find the postgres header files and libraries, which were installed at /usr/pgsql-9.3/lib and /usr/pgsql-9.3/include.  
> 
> I resolved the issue by creating symlinks to one of the places that are checked within the install script, but this is not a very elegant solution.  I also tried modifying the configure.in file to include the paths, but that did not resolve the issue (i.e., those paths were still not checked in the install script).  
> 
> I'm sure it is not possible to deal with all of the different places that Postgres is installed from various package managers and distributions, but I just wanted to make you aware of this particular issue.
> 
> Thanks,
> Ted Rosenbaum
> 
>

messages.subject: Why unrecognized field type?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Apologies for cross-posting this to the RPostrgeSQL and PostGIS mailing
lists, but I'm not sure where the problem lies.

I am using the RPostgreSQL package of R to connect to my installation of
PostgreSQL/PostGIS. I want to retrieve some coordinates from my database
and run the below command. Is this just that R doesn't know what to do with
Geometry's, or is it something I should be more concerned about? I ask, as
I'm having some wider issues with my workflow and this may be related.

Thanks

James

> dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT st_transform(st_setsrid(st_makepoint(soose::numeric, soosn::numeric),27700),4326) FROM stage WHERE ssid = '707187161010202'")


st_transform

postgresqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :

(id:480912) in column 0)

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I run the following query that gives me the error below. I understand that 
RpostgreSQL understands the alias afrobarometer a, gadm2 g as references to 
the schema, but all i want is to be sure it understands what columns in 
which tables i refer to.

res <- dbSendQuery(con,"SELECT a.country, a.region, a.year, a.region2, 
a.gid AS regionid, a.dup, a.trustcops, a.trustcourts, a.corruptioncops, 
a.corruptioncourts, a.paybribe, a.paybribe2, a.paybribe3, a.paybribe4, 
a.paybribe5, a.responsivenessloc, a.tradauthsolconf, a.soctrusmpeop, 
a.soctrusnei, a.soctruseth, a.tradlaw, a.traddisp, a. tradland, 
a.atcomeet.y, a.trustlocal, a.performancelocal, a.tradconthelp, 
a.trusttradauth, a.atcomeeting, a.soctrustrel, a.corruptionlocal , a.year, 
g.geom INTO afrogadm FROM afrobarometergadm a, gadm2 g WHERE g.objectid = 
a.gid;")

Error in postgresqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) : 
  RS-DBI driver: (could not Retrieve the result : ERROR:  schema "a" does 
not exist

Any suggestions?

--
